runtime_summary: Original 72 top-level Go tests across 7 packages passed before authored controls.
Real search controls confirm first-N instead of best-N and stale cache after restored mtime.
Actual EXIF control confirms zero exposure numerator panic, normal exposure positive control works.
Five original CLI controls distinguish source exclusion/TopN omission, unlimited positive, missing directory, corrupt candidate and JPEG-only discovery.
Isolated lifecycle control confirms Close does not cancel registered state. Actual JPEG multipart pre-cancelled request still starts/completes background search.
Four original JS adapter controls confirm delayed start after Stop and false completion statuses; adapters are not browser end-to-end proof.
README root build fails; correct cmd/imgsearch binary builds and served real desktop screens.
takeaways: Maintain recipe/content identity in cache and reject stale source identity; mtime-only claims insufficient.
Keep incomplete, cancelled and successful-empty scans distinguishable.
Apply exclusion before result budget; select best-N across complete admitted candidates.
Use cancellation generation through upload, worker lifetime, publication and UI callbacks.
Keep exact byte/pixel duplicate evidence separate from uncalibrated perceptual scores.
